title: 6 Stocks For 2026 [FULL PODCAST]

recommendations.speaker: Ryan Henderson
recommendations.reasoning: Monopoly in US alternative accommodations with 50%+ exclusive listings vs 17% for Booking. Revenue grew from $2.6B (2017) to $11.1B (2024). 23% operating margins with potential to reach 33%+ like Booking. Strong network effects. 12% annual booking growth projected. $72B EV = 10x 2030 operating income.
recommendations.quote: I would somewhat controversially argue that Airbnb is a monopoly, at least in the United States.

recommendations.speaker: Brett Schaefer
recommendations.reasoning: Stock down 55% in 2025, EV/EBIT now 14x. 464 locations with room for 1,000-2,500. 10%+ revenue growth via unit expansion + 3% comp store sales. 15%+ EPS growth with buybacks. Targets 20% of US population focused on health. Differentiated from Kroger/Walmart with organic/attribute-based focus.
recommendations.quote: If you think that you found a grocery store that's going to maintain 12% comp store sales and grow their store base, that should be your whole portfolio.
recommendations.downside_note: H1 2026 may have weak comp sales due to tough comparisons

recommendations.speaker: Ryan Henderson
recommendations.reasoning: Battleground stock similar to Alphabet narrative in early 2025. AI disruption fears overblown - last mile editing still requires tools. Enterprise customers need interoperability. Partnered with AI models via Firefly. Canva/Figma threat real but Adobe crucial for enterprises.
recommendations.quote: The last mile is still the problem. We're a year forward now and last mile is still the problem.

summary: Episode covers 6 stock picks for 2026, with Ryan and Brett each picking 3 stocks including one short. Key picks are Airbnb (monopoly in alternative accommodations), Sprouts Farmers Market (differentiated grocery down 55%), and Adobe (battleground stock with overblown AI fears). The hosts emphasize emerging moats, simple valuation frameworks, and contrarian thinking.
key_takeaways: Airbnb is a monopoly with 50%+ exclusive listings - target 10x 2030 operating income
Sprouts Farmers Market down 55%, EV/EBIT 14x, 15%+ EPS growth potential
Adobe AI disruption fears overblown - enterprise customers need interoperability
Focus on emerging moats: 'If listings are growing, the moat is widening'
Less than 10x 5-year earnings for high quality businesses
One undisclosed short position - first time publicly discussed
